_notes: FULL-COVERAGE DUMMY SSA-1099 — all 10 writable boxes on Drake's SSA screen carry a
value, so one run proves the whole map at once.
TEN BOXES FOR A FORM WITH TWENTY, and Drake says why on the screen itself. Name,
Beneficiary's SSN, Benefits (Box 3), Benefits repaid (Box 4), Description of amount,
Address and Claim number are printed with an asterisk and NO box to type in, under the
legend: '* No input required since there is no impact on the tax return'. Only Box 5
(the net), the Medicare premiums and the federal withholding change the return.
The keys below that Drake has no box for are still sent ON PURPOSE — beneficiary_name,
benefits_paid, medicare_part_b and the rest. They should come back reported BY NAME as
not-on-this-screen, each with its reason, rather than lumped in as unknown keys. A
dropped identifier has to be loud, and that is the behaviour being proven here.
FIELD 1 IS TS, NOT TSJ. Drake offers T and S only — Social Security belongs to one
person, and a married couple's two statements are TWO RECORDS on this screen, one each.
Field 8's codes carry a LEADING ZERO — '01', not '1' — and are for state returns only.
The amounts are deliberately distinct and nothing like a real statement. This is a TEST
RETURN payload. It is not anybody's tax data.
NOTE ON DUPLICATES: this screen has no payer to dedupe on (the payer is the government),
so the agent cannot tell a spouse's legitimate second record from the same person's
statement going in twice. Entering it twice would double the client's benefits. Check
the TS box before re-running.
Client: the test return 123456789 / fynn, Test.
